top200Peaks.name: Mount Elbert
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Elbert is the highest peak in Colorado and the entire Rocky Mountains, named after Samuel Hitt Elbert, a Colorado statesman.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Massive
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Massive lives up to its name with five summits over 14,000 feet, making it one of the most massive mountains in Colorado.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Harvard
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Harvard is named after Harvard University and is the third highest peak in Colorado, featuring a challenging but non-technical climb.

top200Peaks.name: Blanca Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Blanca Peak is considered one of the four sacred mountains by the Navajo people and features a dramatic 5,000+ foot prominence.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Massive North Summit
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Massive's north summit is one of five summits over 14,000 feet on this massive mountain.

top200Peaks.name: La Plata Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: La Plata Peak, Spanish for 'silver peak', offers stunning views of the Collegiate Peaks and is a popular fourteener climb.

top200Peaks.name: Uncompahgre Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Uncompahgre Peak is the highest summit of the San Juan Mountains and its name means 'hot water spring' in the Ute language.

top200Peaks.name: Crestone Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Crestone Peak is one of the most difficult fourteeners to climb, requiring technical scrambling and route-finding skills.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Lincoln
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Lincoln is often climbed with nearby fourteeners Cameron, Bross, and Democrat in what's called the 'Decalibron' loop.

top200Peaks.name: Grays Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Grays Peak is the highest peak on the Continental Divide in North America and is often climbed with nearby Torreys Peak.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Antero
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Antero is famous among rockhounds for its aquamarine crystals, some of the finest gem-quality specimens in North America.

top200Peaks.name: Torreys Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Torreys Peak is named after botanist John Torrey and forms a popular twin climb with Grays Peak via a connecting ridge.

top200Peaks.name: Castle Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Castle Peak features dramatic castle-like rock formations near its summit and is the highest peak in the Elk Mountains.

top200Peaks.name: Quandary Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Quandary Peak is one of Colorado's most accessible fourteeners, located near Breckenridge, and is a popular winter climb.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Evans
top200Peaks.funFact: Officially renamed Mount Blue Sky in 2023, it features the highest paved road in North America, reaching 14,130 feet.

top200Peaks.name: Longs Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Longs Peak features the famous Diamond face, one of North America's premier alpine rock climbing destinations with over 50 routes.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Wilson
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Wilson is one of the most technical fourteeners, requiring exposed scrambling and often climbed with nearby El Diente Peak.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Cameron
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Cameron is not officially recognized as a separate fourteener by some lists due to low prominence, but is part of the Decalibron loop.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Shavano
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Shavano is famous for the 'Angel of Shavano' snow formation that appears on its east face each spring.

top200Peaks.name: Castle Peak North Summit
top200Peaks.funFact: Castle Peak's north summit offers spectacular views of the Maroon Bells and Pyramid Peak.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Belford
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Belford is often combined with nearby Mount Oxford for a popular fourteener double-summit day hike.

top200Peaks.name: Crestone Needle
top200Peaks.funFact: Crestone Needle is one of the most spectacular fourteeners, featuring knife-edge ridges and exposed Class 3 scrambling.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Princeton
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Princeton overlooks the Princeton Hot Springs and is part of the Collegiate Peaks, a group named after Ivy League universities.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Yale
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Yale is another Collegiate Peak named after Yale University and offers stunning views of the Arkansas River valley.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Bross
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Bross was once home to the Dolly Varden Mine and is now part of the popular Decalibron fourteener loop.

top200Peaks.name: Kit Carson Mountain
top200Peaks.funFact: Kit Carson Mountain is named after the famous frontiersman and requires technical scrambling to reach the summit.

top200Peaks.name: El Diente Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: El Diente means 'the tooth' in Spanish, aptly describing its jagged summit block requiring exposed scrambling.

top200Peaks.name: Maroon Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Maroon Peak and nearby North Maroon are called the 'Deadly Bells' due to unstable rock and numerous climbing accidents.

top200Peaks.name: Tabeguache Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Tabeguache Peak is named after a Ute tribe and is typically climbed in combination with Mount Shavano.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Oxford
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Oxford is another Collegiate Peak and is frequently combined with Mount Belford for an efficient double summit.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Sneffels
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Sneffels is one of the most photographed peaks in Colorado, featured in many car commercials and outdoor magazines.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Democrat
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Democrat completes the Decalibron loop and offers panoramic views of South Park and the Tenmile Range.

top200Peaks.name: Capitol Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Capitol Peak features the infamous 'Knife Edge' ridge and is considered one of the most dangerous fourteeners in Colorado.

top200Peaks.name: Pikes Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Pikes Peak inspired 'America the Beautiful' and hosts the famous Pikes Peak International Hill Climb auto race annually.

top200Peaks.name: Snowmass Mountain
top200Peaks.funFact: Snowmass Mountain features one of Colorado's few remaining glaciers and requires technical climbing skills.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Eolus
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Eolus requires a scenic ride on the Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad to access the trailhead.

top200Peaks.name: Windom Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Windom Peak is part of the remote Chicago Basin trio and requires a multi-day backpacking trip to summit.

top200Peaks.name: Challenger Point
top200Peaks.funFact: Challenger Point was named to honor the crew of Space Shuttle Challenger and is often climbed with Kit Carson.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Columbia
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Columbia is another Collegiate Peak and can be combined with Missouri Mountain for a challenging double summit.

top200Peaks.name: Missouri Mountain
top200Peaks.funFact: Missouri Mountain is named after the Missouri Gulch approach and offers sweeping views of the Sawatch Range.

top200Peaks.name: Humboldt Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Humboldt Peak is named after explorer Alexander von Humboldt and is often climbed with Crestone Peak and Crestone Needle.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Bierstadt
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Bierstadt is one of Colorado's most popular fourteeners, offering an easy hike accessible from Denver in under 2 hours.

top200Peaks.name: Conundrum Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Conundrum Peak is a challenging scramble often combined with Castle Peak via a technical ridge traverse.

top200Peaks.name: Sunlight Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Sunlight Peak requires technical climbing and features one of the most exposed fourteener summits in Colorado.

top200Peaks.name: Handies Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Handies Peak is one of the easiest San Juan fourteeners with a 4WD road reaching nearly 13,000 feet.

top200Peaks.name: Culebra Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Culebra Peak is the only fourteener on private land, requiring permission and a fee to climb.

top200Peaks.name: Ellingwood Point
top200Peaks.funFact: Ellingwood Point is named after Albert Ellingwood, a pioneering Colorado climber who made the first ascent in 1920.

top200Peaks.name: Mount Lindsey
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount Lindsey was originally named Old Baldy but renamed to honor artist Malcom Lindsey.

top200Peaks.name: North Eolus
top200Peaks.funFact: North Eolus is a technical peak in Chicago Basin, often climbed with Mount Eolus via a connecting ridge.

top200Peaks.name: Redcloud Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Redcloud Peak is named for the red color of its volcanic rock and is often paired with Sunshine Peak.

top200Peaks.name: Pyramid Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Pyramid Peak is one of the most technical fourteeners with loose rock and requires advanced scrambling skills.

top200Peaks.name: Wilson Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Wilson Peak is featured on the Coors beer label and requires technical scrambling to reach the summit.

top200Peaks.name: Wetterhorn Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Wetterhorn Peak features dramatic exposure and is considered one of the more challenging San Juan fourteeners.

top200Peaks.name: North Maroon Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: North Maroon Peak forms the iconic Maroon Bells with Maroon Peak, one of the most photographed scenes in Colorado.

top200Peaks.name: San Luis Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: San Luis Peak is the most remote fourteener with a 15-mile round trip hike through beautiful alpine meadows.

top200Peaks.name: Mount of the Holy Cross
top200Peaks.funFact: Mount of the Holy Cross is famous for its distinctive cross-shaped snow pattern visible from the east.

top200Peaks.name: Huron Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Huron Peak is a remote Sawatch fourteener with a long approach but relatively straightforward climbing.

top200Peaks.name: Sunshine Peak
top200Peaks.funFact: Sunshine Peak is the least prominent of all Colorado fourteeners and is usually climbed with Redcloud Peak.

top200Peaks.name: Stewart Peak

top200Peaks.name: Columbia Point
top200Peaks.funFact: Columbia Point is a prominent sub-peak of Mount Columbia.

top200Peaks.name: Tijeras Peak

frontRangePeaks.name: Longs Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Longs Peak is the northernmost fourteener in Colorado and features the famous Diamond face for climbers. It's prominently visible from Denver's northern suburbs.

frontRangePeaks.name: Mount Blue Sky
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans) is the most prominent peak visible from Denver and features the highest paved road in North America. Clearly visible from I-25 and City Park.

frontRangePeaks.name: Pikes Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Pikes Peak inspired Katharine Lee Bates to write 'America the Beautiful' and is visible from Denver on clear days, approximately 70 miles to the south.

frontRangePeaks.name: Grays Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Grays Peak is the highest point on the Continental Divide and is visible from I-70 west of Denver, often climbed with Torreys Peak.

frontRangePeaks.name: Torreys Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Torreys Peak is named after botanist John Torrey and forms a prominent twin with Grays Peak, visible from Denver's western viewpoints.

frontRangePeaks.name: Mount Bierstadt
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Mount Bierstadt is one of the most accessible fourteeners from Denver, visible from the metro area and offering an easy Class 1 hike.

frontRangePeaks.name: Parry Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Parry Peak is visible from I-70 near Winter Park and is named after botanist Charles Christopher Parry.

frontRangePeaks.name: Chief Mountain
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Chief Mountain is a prominent landmark visible from I-70 west of Denver, named for its chief-like profile.

frontRangePeaks.name: Douglas Mountain
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Douglas Mountain is easily visible from I-70 near the Eisenhower Tunnel and offers excellent views of the Continental Divide.

frontRangePeaks.name: North Arapaho Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: North Arapaho Peak is the highest summit in the Indian Peaks Wilderness and is visible from Boulder and northern Denver.

frontRangePeaks.name: South Arapaho Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: South Arapaho Peak is often climbed with its northern twin and offers stunning views of the Indian Peaks.

frontRangePeaks.name: Apache Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Apache Peak is part of the Indian Peaks and is known for its rugged terrain and alpine lakes.

frontRangePeaks.name: Navajo Peak
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Navajo Peak is another prominent Indian Peak visible from Denver and features beautiful alpine terrain.

frontRangePeaks.name: Mount Audubon
frontRangePeaks.funFact: Mount Audubon is named after naturalist John James Audubon and offers one of the easiest thirteener climbs near Denver.
